summary.headline: Pricol Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 23.5% YoY to Rs 1,083.6 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 11.41% on West Asia-driven cost headwinds.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations was about Rs 1,083.58 crore, up 23.46% YoY, with EBITDA of Rs 123.69 crore (11.41% margin) and PAT of Rs 67.02 crore (6.19% margin). Management said EBITDA grew only about 21% YoY because of polymer, LPG, freight, rupee and minimum-wage cost increases, which it expects to recover through quarterly and half-yearly indexation over Q2 and Q3. The call also covered a proposed demerger of the DIS/DICVS business from the ACFMS and polymer businesses, a Rs 700 crore capex cycle, and a one-year pause on M&A.

segments.name: DIS / DICVS (driver information systems, two-wheeler, CV, PV)
segments.commentary: Growth about 25% YoY in Q1 per CEO, equal to ACFMS. Two-wheeler revenue grew 28% vs industry 23%. Targets growth at least 5% above market; two-wheeler DIS volume share 30-35%, CV share about two-thirds, PV share 8-9% (Tata Motors dependent).

segments.name: ACFMS (auto components, fluid management and switches)
segments.commentary: Growth about 25% YoY in Q1 per CEO. Target is 10% growth above market; first switches business won from Suzuki; disc brake production started for a major Indian OEM, with meaningful revenue from FY28.

segments.name: Polymer (plastics)
segments.commentary: Q1 revenue Rs 249 crore at 7.8% EBITDA margin; most affected by polymer and LPG price spikes. Capacity about Rs 1,000 crore turnover today, targeted at about Rs 2,000 crore post capex; management targets 2.5x FY25 base, and sees ROCE muted during capex cycle before 16-18% steady state.

guidance_outlook: Q2 and Q3 FY27 expected to recover delayed earnings via indexation: about 75% of revenue indexed from Q2, balance from Q3 (half-yearly indexation).
EBITDA expected under pressure for next couple of quarters until West Asia-related costs normalise; management said Q1 costs were delayed, not lost.
Minimum wage increases in three states add about Rs 21 crore per annum; customer pass-through still under negotiation.
Steady-state blended EBITDA margin target 12.5-13%; management estimates about 1.5% EBITDA lost in Q1 and about another half of that still recoverable via price increases and indexation.
FY30 (CY30/FY31) revenue ambition of Rs 8,000 crore for DICVS retained; FY30 targets unchanged despite M&A pause.
Demerger expected to take at least 4 quarters, management hopes for 12 months; businesses to operate as separate entities from October and fully by December.
Disc brake and switches revenue to become meaningful only from FY28.
capex_capacity: Rs 700 crore capex cycle over 18-24 months: about Rs 400 crore for polymer (including relocating out of TVS campuses under lock-in), Rs 150-180 crore for DICVS, about Rs 120 crore for ACFMS.
Five new factories being brought on stream: Hosur (state-of-the-art), Mysore, Aurangabad (greenfield), Sanand Gujarat (for Honda), and Bhiwadi/NCR under construction.
Polymer Centre of Excellence to be fully operational by May 2027; in-house tool room being built.
Partnership with BOE for backlight modules for screens in progress.
Polymer capacity expected to support about Rs 2,000 crore turnover from about Rs 1,000 crore today; plants on schedule barring a month or two of delay.
demand_pricing: Industry growth in Q1 about 22-23% weighted average; company grew about 26% overall, outperforming by about 4 points.
Q1 sequentially flat versus Q4, which management said is seasonal; no share loss claimed.
Raw material costs rising sharply for memory-controlled devices due to AI-driven demand; polymer, LPG, crude, freight and rupee all adverse.
Two-wheeler TFT penetration about 7-8% of two-wheelers produced; management expects this to double in 2-3 years.
Polymer customer wins include Ather, River, Simple Energy, Raptee, Honda, Royal Enfield, Suzuki (switches) and Yamaha (final stage); Mahindra engagement started for PV and DICVS.
E-cockpit: proof of concept shown to customers; global competitors have volume advantage of 40-50x, so cost competitiveness limited.

qa_highlights.question: Why demerge the DIS/connected vehicles business from the rest of the group?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the board debated it for over two years; the DIS business needs large investment and technology partners, which investors find hard to back inside a multi-business company. Demerger is intended to allow a debt and equity mix and partner onboarding.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q1 margin outlook and steady state?
qa_highlights.answer: Steady-state blended EBITDA margin of 12.5-13% is the target; Q1 lost about 1.5% of margin; Q2 and Q3 expected to recover through indexation, with about half of the lost margin still recoverable if prices hold.

qa_highlights.question: Capex split and timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Rs 700 crore over 18-24 months: Rs 400 crore polymer, Rs 150-180 crore DICVS, about Rs 120 crore ACFMS.

qa_highlights.question: Timeline for demerger?
qa_highlights.answer: At least 4 quarters per advisers; management hopes for 12 months. Internal operation as separate entities from October, fully by December.

qa_highlights.question: Is M&A still on the cards?
qa_highlights.answer: M&A paused for about one year after due diligence found asset quality issues; FY30 targets unchanged. Will consider only attractive quality assets.

qa_highlights.question: Disc brake revenue and ramp?
qa_highlights.answer: No material revenue yet; meaningful revenue expected only from FY28, consistent with prior guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Polymer business performance in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue Rs 249 crore with EBITDA margin of 7.8%; polymer and LPG cost spikes expected to correct in Q2 and Q3.

financial_highlights.change: Gross margin down ~160 bps (per analyst question, not disputed)
